statement: Points $A$, $B$, $C$ are on a plane with $AB = BC = CA = 6$. At any step, you may choose any three existing points and draw the circumcentre of the triangle they form. Prove that you can draw a point whose distance from some previously drawn point is: (a) greater than $7$; (b) greater than $2019$.
Let $a, b$ be positive integers such that $a + b^3$ is divisible by $a^2 + 3ab + 3b^2 - 1$. Prove that $a^2 + 3ab + 3b^2 - 1$ is divisible by the cube of an integer greater than $1$.

You have a $2m \times 2n$ grid of squares coloured like a standard checkerboard. Find the total number of ways to place $mn$ counters on white squares so that each square contains at most one counter and no two counters occupy diagonally adjacent white squares.

Prove that for $n > 1$ and real numbers $a_0, a_1, \ldots, a_n, k$ with $a_1 = a_{n-1} = 0$,
$$|a_0| - |a_n| \leq \sum_{i=0}^{n-2} |a_i - ka_{i+1} - a_{i+2}|.$$

A 2-player game is played on $n \geq 3$ points in general position (no three collinear). Each move consists of drawing a new segment between two of the points. The first player to draw a segment that creates an odd cycle loses. (An odd cycle must use only the original $n$ points as vertices.) Find all $n$ for which the first player wins.
